cells.tense: You are at the table with the pen, deciding what is fair and what has finished.
cells.ask: Take one thing you are done with and say so out loud, once, to yourself if no one is there — then leave it alone for the day.
cells.core:
You feel what's fair without grinding on it. Someone was done wrong, a stretch ran its course, a weight got carried past its use — you read it straight and act on the read. The feeling is there and it's accurate, and it doesn't eat the whole day.

A friend asks for a hard call and you give it clean. Work ends and you close it without a wake. Something you've held gets put down and the room is better after. That is release doing its job — you know what to feed next before anyone names it, and the next thing has room because you cleared it. The clearing is the point, and you do it without ceremony.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's finished, and you let it finish.
cells.verb: deciding what is fair and what is finished
cells.place: where what is done gets set down

cells.tense: You are living out past the moment where the wrong has not yet been righted, building the case before anyone asks.
cells.ask: Pick one open account and leave it unanswered for a day — no replay, no rehearsal, no preparing the argument.
cells.core:
Fairness is running ahead of the room. Somewhere out there a score sits unsettled and you're already in it — weighing, predicting, holding the verdict ready before the situation has asked for one. You are protecting the scale so hard that the exchange can't happen.

What you're after is real: give and take that feels honest. When it works, a lunch happens and nobody counts. A favor goes back out with no ledger behind it. Someone tells you a thing and you hear it before you decide what it means. You can keep the same care and hold it loosely enough that it carries instead of pressing down. The grip is the only thing that has to move.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for a verdict nobody asked you for.
cells.verb: deciding what is fair and what is finished
cells.place: where what is done gets set down

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, sorting again what you could have said.
cells.ask: Write down one true thing about a situation that has ended, then stop — no letter, no call, no follow-up.
cells.core:
The read is still there but it isn't landing. Something finished and you keep going back over it, turning it for a better angle. The plain sense of what's fair has gone quiet, so the exchange goes whichever way it leaned.

When it works it looks easy. You can tell a fair deal from a bad one and say so without rancor. You hand something back and mean it. A question comes at you and the answer is already there. The way in from here is smaller than a verdict: get clear on one thing, plain and real, and let that clarity do the work today. One true thing is enough to start the current moving again.
cells.sheetLine: You keep turning over what's already behind you.
cells.verb: deciding what is fair and what is finished
cells.place: where what is done gets set down

cells.tense: You are already deciding what is fair and what gets released, and you talk about it as just handling things.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you actually think about one thing you've stayed quiet on, and let the saying be the end of it.
cells.core:
You run the room — what's deserved, what's let go, who gets what — and you don't name it as yours. It comes out as practicality, or as being the one who deals with it. The work is real and it belongs to you and it goes unfiled.

Underneath there's something simpler: a read that arrives before the argument does. You sense what's right and move on it without calling it a decision. Done well it looks like a clean call that surprises no one, and an old debt let go without a speech. The read is already yours. Start with one thing you've been treating as obvious and say it as something you see.
cells.sheetLine: You're already deciding what's fair, and calling it practicality.
cells.verb: deciding what is fair and what is finished
cells.place: where what is done gets set down
